title: Set up smart-home routines by describing them
summary: An open-source project lets Claude Code copy a live Home Assistant setup, write home routines from plain-English requests, and check them several ways before sending changes back.
agent_role: Claude Code edits and validates the configuration locally; the user describes automations, reviews changes and triggers the push over SSH.
what_they_did: A developer, philippb, shared free code that lets Claude Code manage a Home Assistant smart-home setup. The user adds a Home Assistant access key and remote-login details. One command downloads the live settings. Claude Code then writes home routines from plain-English requests. Automatic checks confirm the settings are well formed and that every device named really exists. A second command checks again before uploading the changes to the home system.
worth_knowing: You need Home Assistant's "Advanced SSH & Web Terminal" add-on installed for remote access. The first download replaces the project's sample settings folder with your real settings.
prompt: In this Home Assistant config repo, I want an automation that [describe behavior, e.g. turns on the hallway lights at sunset when someone is home]. First search the entity registry and list the entities you plan to use, so I can confirm them. Then write the YAML in the right config file and run the validation tools for syntax, entity references and HA config checks. Show me the diff and the validation results. Do not run make push until I approve.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
